key_facts: NioCorp Developments signed a preliminary deal to supply Lockheed with 15 metric tons per year of scandium from its Nebraska mine, slated to open by 2028 with annual production of 100 metric tons.
Lockheed is separately negotiating with Teck Resources for germanium supply from Teck's Red Dog mine in Alaska.
Lockheed is also in germanium supply talks with Quebec-based 5N Plus, which received Pentagon funding to process the metal from recycled feedstock in Utah.
The U.S. has not mined scandium since 1969, and Rio Tinto is the only North American scandium producer, at roughly nine metric tons annually.
Trump signed an executive order last month making it harder for defense contractors to obtain waivers allowing them to buy minerals from China and other prohibited foreign suppliers.
